name: Gmail Attachment Saver - Auto-Save Email Attachments to Google Drive

nodes.name: 1. New Email Arrives
nodes.notes: Polls your Gmail every hour for new mail. IMPORTANT: 'Simple' is OFF on purpose - with Simple on, n8n strips attachments out of the trigger output and nothing will ever be saved.

nodes.name: 2. Extract Attachments
nodes.notes: Turns each email into one item per attachment. The file itself travels as binary data named 'data'; sender, subject and message ID travel with it. Emails with no attachments produce no items and the run ends here.

nodes.name: 3. Check Saved Log
nodes.notes: Looks the message ID up in your Attachment Log sheet. Any rows that come back are candidates for 'already saved' - node 4 makes the final call by file name too.

nodes.name: 4. Flag Already Saved
nodes.notes: Marks each attachment already_saved only when BOTH the message ID and the file name are already in the log. Gmail triggers can re-fire on old mail - this flag is what stops duplicate files piling up in Drive.

nodes.name: 5. Already Saved?
nodes.notes: TRUE (top output) = already in Drive, skip it. FALSE (bottom output) = new file, save it.

nodes.name: 5a. Skip - Already in Drive
nodes.notes: Dead end on purpose: this attachment is already in Drive and already logged, so the run stops here for this item.

nodes.name: 6. Rename File
nodes.notes: Builds the Drive file name: date_sender_original-name. Sorted by date, grouped by sender, and two files with the same original name can never overwrite each other.

nodes.name: 7. Save to Google Drive
nodes.notes: Uploads the attachment to your Google Drive. After importing, open this node and pick the destination folder (create one called 'Email Attachments' first if you like) - otherwise files land in your Drive root.

nodes.name: 8. Prepare Log Row
nodes.notes: Combines the Drive result (file ID and link) with the email metadata into the single row that gets written to the log.

nodes.name: 9. Log to Sheet
nodes.notes: Appends one row per saved file to your Attachment Log - the same sheet node 3 checks, which is what makes the dedupe work on the next run.

parameters.content:
## Gmail Attachment Saver - what this does

Every hour this workflow checks your Gmail for new emails, pulls out every attachment, saves each file to Google Drive with a tidy name (date_sender_original-name), and writes one row per file to a Google Sheet so you can find who sent what, and when.

Built for small businesses drowning in emailed invoices, receipts, signed forms and supplier PDFs that currently live - and get lost - inside the inbox.

- No attachment? The email is ignored and nothing is written anywhere.
- Same attachment twice? A log check stops it being saved twice.
- Nothing is deleted, moved or labelled in your Gmail. The workflow only reads.

Honest note: this file is structure-checked - the JSON parses, every connection points at a real node, and the Code nodes were reviewed line by line. It has not been live-import-tested in a running n8n instance, so allow 15 minutes for setup and expect to pick your own folders and sheet on first import.

## Setup (about 15 minutes)

1. Import this JSON into n8n (Workflows -> Import from File).
2. Node 1: connect your Gmail account. Leave 'Simple' OFF - with Simple on, n8n strips attachments out of the trigger output and nothing will ever be saved.
3. Create a Google Sheet called 'Attachment Log' with one tab and these headers in row 1: saved_at | file_name | drive_file_name | sender | subject | message_id | drive_link | drive_id
4. Nodes 3 and 9: connect your Google account and pick that sheet in both. Node 3 reads it (the dedupe check), node 9 appends to it.
5. Node 7: connect Google Drive and pick the folder attachments should land in - create one called 'Email Attachments' first if you like.
6. Save the workflow, then switch it Active (top right). From then on it checks your inbox every hour.

First-run tip: send yourself an email with a PDF attached and watch nodes 2, 7 and 9 light up.

## 1 - Intake

Node 1 polls Gmail every hour. Node 2 unpacks each email into one item per attachment and carries the file itself through as binary data named 'data'. Sender, subject and message ID travel with it - they end up in the file name and the log.

## 2 - Never save the same file twice

Node 3 looks the message ID up in your Attachment Log. Node 4 marks an attachment 'already saved' only when both the message ID and the file name are already logged. Node 5 sends those to a dead end (5a) and lets everything new through. Gmail triggers can re-fire on old mail - this is what stops your Drive filling up with duplicates.

## 3 - Save it, then write it down

Node 6 renames each file to date_sender_original-name, so Drive sorts cleanly and same-name files never overwrite each other. Node 7 uploads the file to your Drive folder. Nodes 8-9 write the log row with the Drive link, so the sheet becomes your searchable index of every attachment you have ever been sent.
